subject: Long tail problem for self-driving data
text:
Hi [NAME],

We recently onboarded Woven by Toyota, who previously lacked a consistent
way to find rare events across millions of miles of driving data. This led
to duplicated engineering efforts and siloed custom tools being built and
maintained across different teams.

I wonder if that resonates with the challenges you've encountered at
[COMPANY], especially as you're testing your self-driving cars in Austin?

In case Encord is new to you - our platform helps autonomous driving teams
like Woven search and filter for long-tail scenarios, while unifying data
curation, annotation, and model evaluation workflows across the
organization. This has been key to standardizing processes and tracking
productivity, as data requirements constantly evolve.

Keen to hear how you're thinking about this at [COMPANY]? I'm flexible Tuesday
to Thursday if you're open to a quick chat.

subject: Shifting to more precise labelling + improving your model performance
text:
Hi [NAME],

Hope you're doing well. Got in touch with your team recently - saw the recent team + funding growth, looks like an exciting time for you guys.

Don't think Encord needs too much of an intro, know you've spoken with the team in the past - but I thought it might be an opportune time to suggest a quick catch-up, show you some of the work we've done on the product since we last spoke.

As you know, we're video first, and so all our efforts are focused on making that tooling best in class - focusing on frame vs clip level annotation, instance segmentation and bringing in some of your own models to pre-label that data.

As you evaluate your current/future tooling needs - would it make sense to chat in the coming week(s)? Tues/Weds is usually good for our engineering team, but happy to work to your schedule.

subject: Training data pipeline for perception systems
text:
Hi [NAME],

We recently onboarded Mytra who was moving from simulation to real-world
data to train their perception model. At the time they lacked a system to
effectively index, auto-label and QA to keep up with the surging data
volume. I wonder if you're encountering/anticipating similar challenges at
Saronic as you set out roadmaps for your new ASVs?

For context - we help physical AI teams (e.g. Skydio, Zipline, Mytra, etc.)
automate their annotation pipelines as they scale. Handful of customers in
the space leverage our model-assisted workflow and our labelling editor's
native support across 2D (image & video) and 3D point cloud data, as a
complement to Foxglove.

Keen to hear how you're thinking about your training data as you scale? I'm
flexible Tuesdays to Thursdays if you're open to chat.

subject: LBM 2.0?
text:
Hey [NAME]​,

Read the recent write-up of TRI's LBM study & was curious to understand how the team is thinking about further fine-tuning - so thought it'd be a good opportunity to introduce myself. 

I lead a Physical AI / Robotics team here at Encord, working with Woven (who I know you'll be very familiar with), Pickle Robot, Archetype AI & other leading teams - providing the platform to support the fine-tuning of Multimodal foundation models with strong support for video tracking & VLA annotations.

Curious to know if scaling training data pipelines is likely to be a priority as the team further improves its LBMs? 

Let me know if it makes sense to chat, happy to give some ideas based on how we're working with similar teams,
